title: Formal error adjustment raised the deep-minus-shallow non-double-couple contrast in GCMT Mw 5.8+ events in 1982-2020
abstract: In 7,541 selected Global CMT events, the adjusted mean non-double-couple measure was 2.26 percentage points higher for deep than shallow earthquakes (95% three-year block interval +0.27 to +4.57). The model without formal-error terms gave -0.06 points (-1.92 to +1.95). The positive conditional contrast depends on the model and sample: the FREE-depth-only interval includes zero. This result does not establish a physical difference in rupture. We used the fixed January 1976-December 2020 catalog, centroid depth groups below 70 km, 70 to below 300 km, and at least 300 km, and positive errors for all six tensor entries. The primary model includes magnitude, year, station sum and formal relative error. The Mw at least 6.5 check gave +6.45 points (+4.24 to +8.85). Formal errors omit Earth-model error, and geographic and source differences remain. The package includes original code, aggregate evidence and a figure. External event data remain outside the baseline publication.

display.caption: Catalog mean measures and adjusted deep-minus-shallow contrasts. Bars on the right show 95% three-year block intervals. The formal-error and depth-flag choices affect the conclusion.

citations.reason: Synthetic inversions show that Earth-model mismatch can create apparent non-double-couple components.
Global CMT method and 2004 method change.
Depth-boundary audit motivates separate checks of method eras and depth flags. No code or derived data reused.
